title: Sustainable Investment Policies via Opponent Shaping
one_liner: By secretly nudging how agents learn, you can guide self-interested investors toward climate-friendly choices without changing their goals.
lead: Investors chasing quick profits ignore climate risk, creating a tragedy of the commons: everyone acts rationally for themselves, but the group sinks. This paper shows how to secretly reshape the way agents learn so they naturally discover cooperation is in their own interest. The technique is called Advantage Alignment. It works by reweighting the learning signal agents receive so that cooperation-friendly choices produce higher learning rewards than selfish choices, even when the direct payoff is slightly lower. Over time, agents follow this altered signal and converge on cooperation because, in a cooperative equilibrium, everyone earns higher long-term returns together than alone.

paras: Climate change hurts everyone in the long term, but it pays to ignore it today. An investor who cuts carbon investments loses money this quarter while competitors gain market share. So every rational investor waits for others to move first—and nobody moves. This is the prisoner's dilemma on a global scale: individual incentives pull against collective welfare.

A naive policy might just mandate: all investors must favor green projects. But mandates break if investors can cheat or find loopholes. The real problem is deeper: the agents' own learning process is driving them toward short-term greed. To fix the outcome, you have to fix how they learn.

callout.html: Reshape the learning incentives of self-interested agents so they converge toward cooperation without changing what they claim to want.

panels.title: 1. The setup
panels.viz_args: Company stock price vs. carbon cost
panels.caption: Investors see two paths: short-term profit or long-term climate safety. Only profit pays today.

panels.title: 2. The trap
panels.caption: All investors independently pick profit. It looks rational locally but leaves everyone worse off.

panels.title: 3. Hidden shaping
panels.caption: Advantage Alignment reweights the learning signal agents receive without changing stated goals.

panels.title: 4. Learning shifts
panels.caption: Shaped agents discover that picking safety actually leads to better long-term returns for everyone.

panels.title: 5. Escape the trap
panels.caption: Cooperation emerges as the rational choice. Coordination problem solved by steering learning.

steps.text: Characterize the intertemporal dilemma: when do individual incentives diverge from collective welfare mathematically.
Identify which decisions lead to better shared outcomes versus what agents naturally choose without shaping, because only then can the algorithm amplify good choices and dampen bad ones.
Adjust the learning signal each agent receives so cooperation pays off in their own updates.
Without knowing they are being shaped, they update their strategy based on the altered signal.
Agents converge to a strategy that serves both self-interest and collective good simultaneously.

paras: The paper changes one thing: the learning signal that tells each agent whether its decision was good or bad. By secretly reweighting this signal, agents discover that the collectively good choice is also the individually smart choice.

hidden.name: Individual-vs-collective advantage gap
paras: The hidden quantity is the gap between the reward that tells an agent its choice was good for itself, and the true impact that choice had on the entire group. In the tragedy, agents get high individual rewards for choices that tank the collective outcome. The paper measures this gap: where individual and collective interests diverge, the signal is being twisted.

Advantage Alignment uses this gap to forge a new learning signal where individual rewards track collective welfare instead. By reweighting outcomes, the paper nudges the agent's self-interested learning direction toward the cooperation zone instead of the trap.

heat.caption: Darker means stronger mismatch between selfish and collective payoffs; highlight shows the gap the paper exploits.

reads.html: The paper notices: agents learn from the wrong scoreboard. Fix the scoreboard, and selfish learning chases collective good.

Advantage Alignment computes the signed advantage (reward for an action minus the baseline), then biases it toward outcomes that lift all boats. Agents follow the modified reward signal, naturally converging to socially beneficial equilibria.

paras: Agents learn by following a path that increases their reward score. That path is drawn by the reward signal: do action A if it increases payoff, do action B if it pays more. The tragedy happens because the reward signal reflects immediate profit, not what is good for the group.

Advantage Alignment rewrites that signal. It doesn't lie to agents about what profits they will get; it changes how they weight different actions during learning. For actions that look individually profitable but wreck collective welfare, the algorithm penalizes them in the learning update. For actions that sacrifice a little individual profit but unlock cooperation, the algorithm amplifies them. Agents follow this rewritten signal naturally—they still think they are chasing their own interest, but the scoreboard they are reading has been quietly rerouted to point toward cooperation. Over time, they discover that cooperation pays for themselves too, because in an equilibrium where everyone cooperates, everyone does better than in the tragedy-of-commons equilibrium.

math.words: shaped reward equals individual reward plus a term that bonuses actions leading to high collective welfare and penalizes actions leading to low collective welfare, scaled by how much the agent cares about alignment
symbols: the learning reward the agent actually receives (the modified signal)
the direct payoff from the action (profit from the investment)
how strongly the algorithm steers toward cooperation (a tuning knob: 0 means no shaping, high means strong pressure)
how much the action benefits the entire group over time
the payoff if everyone does the status quo (the tragedy outcome)

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Scenario: investor chooses a carbon-heavy stock.
V_collective = -8 (group long-term harm outweighs short gain).
The shaped reward is negative; the agent learns to avoid this action.
Second scenario: investor chooses a green stock.
The shaped reward is strongly positive; the agent learns to favor this action.
Same 4-point profit difference, but shaped learning flips the direction.

math.note: The reweighting term vanishes (becomes zero) when individual and collective interests align, so the shaping only bites where they diverge—exactly where the trap is.

charts.title: Without shaping
charts.note: Agents chase immediate returns, wrecking the commons. Individually rational but collectively awful.

charts.title: With Advantage Alignment
charts.note: Shaped learning redirects agents toward choices that lift both their own long-term returns and collective welfare. Cooperation emerges naturally.

items.html: If agents learn that their rewards are being manipulated, they may reject the learning signal or work around it. The algorithm works best when agents do not know they are being shaped.
If alpha is too high, agents may learn to pursue cooperation even when they could defect and win. The shaping must balance: steer toward cooperation without making individual profit irrelevant.

items.b: Collective welfare is hard to measure.
items.html: The algorithm needs a clear signal of whether an action helps or hurts the group, because if the signal is wrong, agents learn the wrong lesson. In real markets, that signal is buried in noise and takes years to manifest, making it hard for the algorithm to steer correctly.
Tune alpha so agents naturally discover that cooperation is in their self-interest, measure collective impact honestly, and ensure agents cannot detect or circumvent the shaping.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Implement a small three-agent investment game where each agent picks green or dirty projects. Give each agent a profit score (higher for dirty, lower for green). Without shaping, all three agents converge to dirty projects and share low long-term welfare. Then apply Advantage Alignment with alpha tuned so the individual profit from cooperating still leads to learning toward cooperation. Run training and show that all three agents learn to pick green, not because they value the environment, but because the shaped reward signal makes that profitable to them individually. Verify that the shaped signal correctly bonuses cooperation-friendly actions and penalizes tragedy-inducing actions.
demo.metric_eq: cooperation_rate = (count of agents picking green projects) / (total agents); welfare = (average long-term return across all agents)
demo.closing: The demo must show that agents self-interest and collective good align after shaping, even though they started in opposition.
